#### `modules/graphics-ext/include/CNA/Graphics/FilmGrainPass.hpp`

| ID | Line | Access/kind | C++ symbol | C mapping | Tests | Status |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CPP-DFB41B019792` | 33 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::FilmGrainPass` | One `cna_<pass>_create` each plus the pass's own accessors, on `CBIND-089B`'s helpers.  **Two of the nine are not passes, and finding that out was the slice.** `DecalPass` and `SpatialUpscalePass` are named "Pass" and were counted among the seventeen, but neither derives from `PostProcessPass`: they have no `apply`, and each is driven by its own `draw` with explicit sizes rather than by a chain. The compiler said so -- their `shared_ptr` would not convert -- which is the only reason it was caught before the shape was wrong in the ABI. They carry their own handles (`CNA_DecalPassHandle`, `CNA_SpatialUpscalePassHandle`), their own object kinds and their own destroy, and the shared `cna_post_process_pass_*` routes correctly **refuse** them.  `AsciiPass::getEffect` lends the pass's own effect. Binding it needed the resource type behind `CNA_AsciiPostProcessEffectHandle` to be **shared between two translation units** rather than redeclared: two units that register or read one `ObjectKind` must agree on the type it holds, and a second local declaration would compile, register under the same kind, and then be cast to the wrong type -- undefined behaviour no test would reliably catch. `AsciiEffectResource` moved to `CnaCApiGraphicsExtDetail.hpp` for that reason, which is a deliberate structural change rather than a side effect.  **`FxaaPass` corrects nothing**, while the settings bag that can drive the same number floors it at `CNA_RENDER_PIPELINE_MINIMUM_FXAA_EDGE_THRESHOLD_EXT`. Two surfaces, one value, only one correcting -- asserted on both rather than assumed consistent. `DecalPass::setCamera` ignores a non-positive far plane by guarding the whole assignment, so the previous camera survives. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 29, which asserts the shared pass routes **refuse** the two standalone objects and accept the seven real passes -- the only way a caller learns the difference from outside. Proved to execute by asserting the shared destroy accepts a `DecalPass`, which moves the exit code to stage 29 on both arms. Every correcting field is written out of range at both ends against its own bound; `FxaaPass`'s free field is checked against the settings bag's floor in the same stage. The ASCII effect borrow is taken, released, and the pass then still answers. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-089D`) |

| `CPP-7473775AC5FA` | 31 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::FrustumCullerEXT` | `cna_frustum_culler_ext_*` over its own owned handle, created **without a device** because the canonical class has none. **Nothing here refuses** beyond null arguments: it has no shader and no state that can be wrong.  The two `isVisible` overloads and the two `cull` overloads become four separately named routes, since C has no overloading and each answers a different question about a different shape. The index culls hand back **indices into the caller's array** rather than copies.  **`cullTransforms` keeps a transform that has no matching bound**, because the canonical test is `i >= bounds.size() \|\| visible(bounds[i])`. A shorter bounds array therefore means "these ones are always visible", not "cull them" -- the opposite of what a caller who passed a short array by accident would expect, which is why the header states it and the test asserts it with zero bounds. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 39: the frustum is built two ways (camera pair and combined matrix) and shown to give the same matrix; a box in front and a box far behind are asserted to answer **differently**, so a culler that always says yes fails; and three transforms with zero bounds are asserted to return **all three**. Break-proved by asserting none instead, which moves both CNAEXT trees. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-092C`) |

#### `modules/graphics-ext/include/CNA/Graphics/FxaaPass.hpp`

| ID | Line | Access/kind | C++ symbol | C mapping | Tests | Status |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CPP-A5D8661F6CAB` | 36 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::FxaaPass` | One `cna_<pass>_create` each plus the pass's own accessors, on `CBIND-089B`'s helpers.  **Two of the nine are not passes, and finding that out was the slice.** `DecalPass` and `SpatialUpscalePass` are named "Pass" and were counted among the seventeen, but neither derives from `PostProcessPass`: they have no `apply`, and each is driven by its own `draw` with explicit sizes rather than by a chain. The compiler said so -- their `shared_ptr` would not convert -- which is the only reason it was caught before the shape was wrong in the ABI. They carry their own handles (`CNA_DecalPassHandle`, `CNA_SpatialUpscalePassHandle`), their own object kinds and their own destroy, and the shared `cna_post_process_pass_*` routes correctly **refuse** them.  `AsciiPass::getEffect` lends the pass's own effect. Binding it needed the resource type behind `CNA_AsciiPostProcessEffectHandle` to be **shared between two translation units** rather than redeclared: two units that register or read one `ObjectKind` must agree on the type it holds, and a second local declaration would compile, register under the same kind, and then be cast to the wrong type -- undefined behaviour no test would reliably catch. `AsciiEffectResource` moved to `CnaCApiGraphicsExtDetail.hpp` for that reason, which is a deliberate structural change rather than a side effect.  **`FxaaPass` corrects nothing**, while the settings bag that can drive the same number floors it at `CNA_RENDER_PIPELINE_MINIMUM_FXAA_EDGE_THRESHOLD_EXT`. Two surfaces, one value, only one correcting -- asserted on both rather than assumed consistent. `DecalPass::setCamera` ignores a non-positive far plane by guarding the whole assignment, so the previous camera survives. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 29, which asserts the shared pass routes **refuse** the two standalone objects and accept the seven real passes -- the only way a caller learns the difference from outside. Proved to execute by asserting the shared destroy accepts a `DecalPass`, which moves the exit code to stage 29 on both arms. Every correcting field is written out of range at both ends against its own bound; `FxaaPass`'s free field is checked against the settings bag's floor in the same stage. The ASCII effect borrow is taken, released, and the pass then still answers. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-089D`) |

| `CPP-D38D45707622` | 33 | public struct | `CNA::Graphics::GltfMaterialTexturesEXT` | `cna_gltf_material_bridge_build_material` and `_build_extensions`, over four versioned PODs: `CNA_GltfMaterialTexturesEXT`, `CNA_GltfMaterialExtensionTexturesEXT` and the two source structures with their `_init` routines.  **The canonical bridge is written against a C++20 *concept*, not a type**, so that the importer's own record satisfies it without this layer knowing that record. A concept has no C form and is not a callable operation, so the C bridge takes a structure that names exactly the members each concept requires, and the implementation builds a local type from it to meet the constraint. The concept stays the contract; the structure is how C reaches it.  **One value is not carried exactly, and that is canonical rather than a limit of the binding:** glTF's `baseColorFactor` is four floats and a material's albedo is a `Color`, so it is quantised to eight bits per channel. Everything else round-trips. The `_init` routines fill the glTF specification's own defaults -- 1.0 metallic and roughness, 1.5 IOR, 0.5 alpha cutoff -- not this layer's, because an omitted glTF factor means the specification's value.  Textures are borrowed, never owned. An undefined alpha mode is refused rather than cast through into the material, the same rule every enum identity in this ABI follows. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 23, which asserts the glTF defaults rather than this layer's, sees the base-colour quantisation with a fractional value (1.0 would survive any quantiser), refuses a malformed structure and an undefined alpha mode, and builds extensions whose transmission predicate then reports true. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses, the two `_init` routines included -- a caller that can fill a source but not use it has been told nothing useful. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-087D`) |

The C layer mirrors the private `culled_` flag on exactly the two transitions the canonical class uses (set by a successful cull, cleared by an upload) so the answer can say what it means.  `draw` issues an indirect draw against **whatever mesh is bound**; the culler owns the instances and the command, not the geometry. `read_visible_count_ext` answers zero before a cull rather than refusing -- a count is a number. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 39, both arms keyed on the measured support. The reachable success arm is the zero-instance draw, where the canonical body returns before touching the device -- asserting a drawing draw would assert that the fixture had a mesh, not that the route works. |---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CPP-7E9FB22ADD0C` | 40 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::HeightFogPass` | One `cna_<pass>_create` each plus the pass's own accessors, on `CBIND-089B`'s `CreateEnginePass<T>`/`WithEnginePass<T>` helpers reused unchanged -- which is what makes four more passes a table rather than four more designs. The shared base stays with `CBIND-084`; the three per-pass constants become macros with a `static_assert`.  **The guards here are not interchangeable, and that is the whole slice.** Four setters guard with `if (value >= 0)` and **accept zero** -- no fog, no shafts and no aerial perspective are all legitimate settings -- while `VolumetricFogPass::setRange` and `HeightFogPass::setFalloff` guard with `if (value > 0)` and **reject zero as well**, because a zero range has no volume to march and a zero falloff is a division by zero. A shared "negatives are ignored" reading would have got two of the six wrong.  Two more bounds are unusual enough to name. `setTurbidity` floors at **one**, not zero: turbidity is a ratio against a perfectly clear atmosphere, so below one describes air clearer than vacuum. `setAnisotropy` clamps to **-0.95 through 0.95** -- the only two-sided clamp in this phase with a negative lower bound, because scattering runs from fully backward to fully forward and both poles are singular. `HeightFogPass::setBaseHeight` corrects nothing, because a fog base below the origin is legitimate.  `setLight` takes a borrowed shadow map; `CNA_INVALID_HANDLE` means march unshadowed rather than being an error. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 28, which asserts each guard's own bound -- a valid value, then zero, then a negative -- so the `>= 0` and `> 0` guards are told apart rather than assumed alike. Proved to matter by asserting the range guard admits zero the way the density beside it does, which moves the exit code to stage 28 on both arms. The three pure functions are checked by their **relationships** rather than by duplicating their maths: air mass grows with distance, transmittance falls as air mass grows, and optical depth is exactly zero at zero distance and grows with both distance and density. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-089C`) |

#### `modules/graphics-ext/include/CNA/Graphics/InstancedRendererEXT.hpp`

| ID | Line | Access/kind | C++ symbol | C mapping | Tests | Status |

| `CPP-022FE10B1865` | 44 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::InstancedRendererEXT` | `cna_instanced_renderer_ext_*` over its own owned handle. The mesh part is **borrowed** and retained by the resource, so releasing the part handle mid-frame cannot dangle.  **Whether instancing happens is a renderer question, and the answer is not a refusal.** With the fallback enabled a device without instancing draws each instance separately -- the same picture, more slowly. `did_last_draw_instance` and `get_last_draw_call_count` say which happened and what it cost, and like the particle system's compute flag they are records written by `draw` rather than predictions.  With the fallback **disabled**, drawing on such a renderer is refused -- and so is drawing through an effect that cannot carry a per-instance transform, because a per-instance world matrix has nowhere else to go. Both canonical refusals are `logic_error` and both arrive as `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE`: the layer is present and the arguments are fine, this combination of renderer, setting and effect is not.  The two static declarations become element-copy plus stride routes rather than handles, because a shared static declaration has no owner to hand out. They exist because a caller building its own instance buffer must reproduce the layout **exactly**, and copying the elements is how it can check that rather than assume it. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 38. The instance declaration is asserted element by element -- four `Vector4`s sixteen bytes apart at `TextureCoordinate` usage indices one through four, stride sixty-four -- because "describe it identically" is the whole contract. The capacity is asserted **never to shrink** when fewer instances are uploaded, which is what makes a varying instance count allocation-free after the largest frame; zero instances is asserted to succeed. Both boolean setters refuse a non-canonical byte. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-092B`) |

#### `modules/graphics-ext/include/CNA/Graphics/LensFlarePass.hpp`

| ID | Line | Access/kind | C++ symbol | C mapping | Tests | Status |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CPP-CA7A11CEC1A4` | 34 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::LensFlarePass` | One `cna_<pass>_create` each plus the pass's own accessors, on `CBIND-089B`'s helpers.  **Two of the nine are not passes, and finding that out was the slice.** `DecalPass` and `SpatialUpscalePass` are named "Pass" and were counted among the seventeen, but neither derives from `PostProcessPass`: they have no `apply`, and each is driven by its own `draw` with explicit sizes rather than by a chain. The compiler said so -- their `shared_ptr` would not convert -- which is the only reason it was caught before the shape was wrong in the ABI. They carry their own handles (`CNA_DecalPassHandle`, `CNA_SpatialUpscalePassHandle`), their own object kinds and their own destroy, and the shared `cna_post_process_pass_*` routes correctly **refuse** them.  `AsciiPass::getEffect` lends the pass's own effect. Binding it needed the resource type behind `CNA_AsciiPostProcessEffectHandle` to be **shared between two translation units** rather than redeclared: two units that register or read one `ObjectKind` must agree on the type it holds, and a second local declaration would compile, register under the same kind, and then be cast to the wrong type -- undefined behaviour no test would reliably catch. `AsciiEffectResource` moved to `CnaCApiGraphicsExtDetail.hpp` for that reason, which is a deliberate structural change rather than a side effect.  **`FxaaPass` corrects nothing**, while the settings bag that can drive the same number floors it at `CNA_RENDER_PIPELINE_MINIMUM_FXAA_EDGE_THRESHOLD_EXT`. Two surfaces, one value, only one correcting -- asserted on both rather than assumed consistent. `DecalPass::setCamera` ignores a non-positive far plane by guarding the whole assignment, so the previous camera survives. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 29, which asserts the shared pass routes **refuse** the two standalone objects and accept the seven real passes -- the only way a caller learns the difference from outside. Proved to execute by asserting the shared destroy accepts a `DecalPass`, which moves the exit code to stage 29 on both arms. Every correcting field is written out of range at both ends against its own bound; `FxaaPass`'s free field is checked against the settings bag's floor in the same stage. The ASCII effect borrow is taken, released, and the pass then still answers. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-089D`) |

| `CPP-AE6384CE6F9A` | 49 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::LightProbeBaker` | `cna_light_probe_baker_*` over its own owned handle, with the canonical `SceneDraw` becoming `CNA_LightProbeSceneDrawCallback` -- a function pointer plus a `void*` context, the shape every other callback in this ABI uses.  **Whether a baker can bake is probed, not asked**, and the binding preserves that: no renderer publishes "can bind an offscreen target and read it back", and the two do not come together, so the canonical constructor renders one capture and remembers the result. The bake routes refuse an unsupported renderer with `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE` rather than `CNA_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED`, because the layer *is* present and the arguments *are* fine -- NOT_SUPPORTED would collide with "built without the layer" and send a caller to look at its build flags.  A null callback is refused **before** the support check and on every renderer: a bake that draws nothing produces a perfectly valid probe, and a caller could not tell it from a mistake. `setPlanes` is validated and refused as a **pair**, with no clamping -- a silently corrected capture range gives probes that look plausible and are lit from the wrong depth. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 33, which runs **both arms keyed on the measured support**: EasyGL takes the success path and counts six callback invocations per probe (twelve for a two-probe volume), headless takes the refusal path and asserts nothing was drawn. Four bad plane pairs are refused and both halves shown unchanged afterwards; the six faces are refused at both ends. Break-proved in both directions. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-091B`) |

| `CPP-BE9D087B4CD7` | 39 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::LightProbeEXT` | `cna_light_probe_ext_*` over its own owned handle. The probe is a value in C++ and stays a value here: `cna_light_probe_ext_copy_from` and `cna_light_probe_ext_equals` exist so a caller can do through the handle what assignment and comparison do through the object, and `cna_light_probe_volume_ext_set_probe` **copies** rather than borrows -- a volume that aliased its source would change under a caller who later scaled that probe.  The nine-coefficient table is reached one entry at a time and in bulk (`cna_light_probe_ext_copy_coefficients`, which reports the count it needs when the buffer is too small). `kCoefficientCount` and the six visibility directions become `CNA_LIGHT_PROBE_COEFFICIENT_COUNT_EXT` and `CNA_LIGHT_PROBE_VISIBILITY_DIRECTIONS_EXT`, and every index route refuses an index outside its table rather than clamping: a clamped index answers with a *different* coefficient, so the surface lights almost right, which is worse than an error.  Two behaviours read like refusals and are not, and are bound as answers because that is what the bodies do. `visibilityWeight` answers **1.0** -- "nothing known to be in the way" -- both when the probe carries no visibility data and when the distance is not positive; and the two visibility distances are floored at zero rather than refused. `irradiance` is likewise clamped non-negative however the coefficients reconstruct.  The two comparison operators map to the same `cna_light_probe_ext_equals` -- `operator!=` is its negation, and a separate route for "not equal" would be a second name for one answer. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 32: every coefficient round-trips, both ends of both index ranges are refused, the two not-refusals above are asserted as successes returning 1.0, a copy compares equal until one `scale` breaks it, and a probe written into a volume is shown not to follow its source. The layer-absent build asserts each route refuses and leaves its output untouched. The two operators are covered by the same equality assertions, in both directions. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-091A`) |

| `CPP-EA1568B9440E` | 42 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::LightShaftPass` | One `cna_<pass>_create` each plus the pass's own accessors, on `CBIND-089B`'s `CreateEnginePass<T>`/`WithEnginePass<T>` helpers reused unchanged -- which is what makes four more passes a table rather than four more designs. The shared base stays with `CBIND-084`; the three per-pass constants become macros with a `static_assert`.  **The guards here are not interchangeable, and that is the whole slice.** Four setters guard with `if (value >= 0)` and **accept zero** -- no fog, no shafts and no aerial perspective are all legitimate settings -- while `VolumetricFogPass::setRange` and `HeightFogPass::setFalloff` guard with `if (value > 0)` and **reject zero as well**, because a zero range has no volume to march and a zero falloff is a division by zero. A shared "negatives are ignored" reading would have got two of the six wrong.  Two more bounds are unusual enough to name. `setTurbidity` floors at **one**, not zero: turbidity is a ratio against a perfectly clear atmosphere, so below one describes air clearer than vacuum. `setAnisotropy` clamps to **-0.95 through 0.95** -- the only two-sided clamp in this phase with a negative lower bound, because scattering runs from fully backward to fully forward and both poles are singular. `HeightFogPass::setBaseHeight` corrects nothing, because a fog base below the origin is legitimate.  `setLight` takes a borrowed shadow map; `CNA_INVALID_HANDLE` means march unshadowed rather than being an error. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 28, which asserts each guard's own bound -- a valid value, then zero, then a negative -- so the `>= 0` and `> 0` guards are told apart rather than assumed alike. Proved to matter by asserting the range guard admits zero the way the density beside it does, which moves the exit code to stage 28 on both arms. The three pure functions are checked by their **relationships** rather than by duplicating their maths: air mass grows with distance, transmittance falls as air mass grows, and optical depth is exactly zero at zero distance and grows with both distance and density. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-089C`) |

| `CPP-D196023EB1CF` | 18 | public enum-value | `CNA::Graphics::LodSelectionMode::Distance` | `cna_lod_group_ext_*` over its own owned handle, with `CNA_LodLevelEXT` for a level and `CNA_LodSelectionMode` at the canonical ordinals. The group needs **no graphics device** -- it is a list and a rule, and nothing in it touches one -- so its create route takes none.  **Index zero is always the finest level, in both selection modes**, and the group re-sorts on every change to keep it so: a distance threshold grows as detail falls and a pixel-radius threshold shrinks, so changing the mode reverses the order. That is why `set_selection_mode` also forgets the last selection. A binding that stored the mode without re-sorting would pass every single-mode assertion and silently invert the order for anyone who switched.  Several behaviours are answers rather than refusals: an empty group selects `-1`, a negative distance is **clamped to zero** (a camera behind the object is a position, not a mistake), a level may deliberately hold **no part**, and `projected_radius_pixels` answers the largest representable float at or behind the eye -- "as large as it gets", which picks the finest level rather than none. `set_hysteresis` floors at zero; `set_screen_space_parameters` is validated and refused as a **group**, with the field of view exclusive at both ends.  The group holds raw `ModelMeshPart` pointers, so the C layer remembers which handle each came from and hands **the caller's own handle** back rather than wrapping the pointer in a fresh one -- a fresh handle would be a second owner of something the group only borrows. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 38. The re-sort is asserted by adding three levels out of order, reading them back in `Distance` order, switching to `ScreenSpaceError`, and reading back the **reversed** order -- break-proved by asserting the unsorted order instead, which moves both CNAEXT trees. The screen-space triple is refused four ways and the previous projection shown unchanged after each; pi itself is asserted refused rather than clamped. Selection is asserted to hand back the caller's own part handle. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-092B`) |

| `CPP-D29CC3CE684F` | 35 | public method | `CNA::Graphics::applyMaterial(const PbrMaterial &material, Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Graphics::PbrEffect &effect)` | `cna_pbr_effect_apply_material` and `cna_skinned_pbr_effect_apply_material` for the two `applyMaterial` overloads, `cna_pbr_effect_extract_material` and `cna_skinned_pbr_effect_extract_material` for the two `extractMaterial` overloads, and `cna_pbr_material_apply_state`. Each carries the **full** `CNA_PbrMaterialEXT`, not the smaller `CNA_PbrMaterial`, so every canonical field crosses. The overloads become named routes because C has none, and the concrete effect type is checked at the boundary: applying a PBR material to a `BasicEffect` is an argument error rather than a silent no-op. | `CPP-5931F31E906E` | 38 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::MotionBlurPass` | One `cna_<pass>_create` each plus the pass's own accessors, on `CBIND-089B`'s helpers.  **Two of the nine are not passes, and finding that out was the slice.** `DecalPass` and `SpatialUpscalePass` are named "Pass" and were counted among the seventeen, but neither derives from `PostProcessPass`: they have no `apply`, and each is driven by its own `draw` with explicit sizes rather than by a chain. The compiler said so -- their `shared_ptr` would not convert -- which is the only reason it was caught before the shape was wrong in the ABI. They carry their own handles (`CNA_DecalPassHandle`, `CNA_SpatialUpscalePassHandle`), their own object kinds and their own destroy, and the shared `cna_post_process_pass_*` routes correctly **refuse** them.  `AsciiPass::getEffect` lends the pass's own effect. Binding it needed the resource type behind `CNA_AsciiPostProcessEffectHandle` to be **shared between two translation units** rather than redeclared: two units that register or read one `ObjectKind` must agree on the type it holds, and a second local declaration would compile, register under the same kind, and then be cast to the wrong type -- undefined behaviour no test would reliably catch. `AsciiEffectResource` moved to `CnaCApiGraphicsExtDetail.hpp` for that reason, which is a deliberate structural change rather than a side effect.  **`FxaaPass` corrects nothing**, while the settings bag that can drive the same number floors it at `CNA_RENDER_PIPELINE_MINIMUM_FXAA_EDGE_THRESHOLD_EXT`. Two surfaces, one value, only one correcting -- asserted on both rather than assumed consistent. `DecalPass::setCamera` ignores a non-positive far plane by guarding the whole assignment, so the previous camera survives. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 29, which asserts the shared pass routes **refuse** the two standalone objects and accept the seven real passes -- the only way a caller learns the difference from outside. Proved to execute by asserting the shared destroy accepts a `DecalPass`, which moves the exit code to stage 29 on both arms. Every correcting field is written out of range at both ends against its own bound; `FxaaPass`'s free field is checked against the settings bag's floor in the same stage. The ASCII effect borrow is taken, released, and the pass then still answers. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-089D`) |

Every correcting field is written out of range at both ends against its own bound; `FxaaPass`'s free field is checked against the settings bag's floor in the same stage. A binding that clamped in the setter would look friendlier and would make `get_settings` lie about what it was given.  **`uses_compute` records what the last `update` did, not what the next one will do** -- it is written inside `update` and nowhere else, so `set_simulation_on_cpu_ext` does not change the answer until an update runs. The header says so, because asking it immediately after switching is the natural mistake.  Falling back to the CPU is a **success** path here, unlike GPU culling: the CPU path produces the same particles, only more slowly. Forcing it **carries the particles across** rather than restarting them, and setting the value it already has does nothing at all.  The two value initializers refuse without the engine layer, unlike `CNA_AreaLightEXT`'s and `CNA_ImageBasedLightEXT`'s -- the difference is where the canonical header lives, not whether the type is a POD. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 37 and the layer-absent block. The `uses_compute` ordering is asserted by stepping the simulation between the switch and the query. The carry-across is asserted by reading a particle before forcing the CPU and finding it unchanged after. The static hash is asserted deterministic *and* seed-sensitive, so a constant would fail. Break-proved in both directions. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-092A`) |

| `CPP-E5594F42A270` | 39 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::PbrMaterialExtensions` | `cna_pbr_material_extensions_*` over an owned handle. The canonical type is a **value** -- it compares, hashes and prints by content -- but it holds nine borrowed `Texture2D` pointers, so it is bound as a handle rather than a C structure: a plain structure would put raw texture pointers in caller-writable memory. It never owns a texture given to it, which is the borrow rule this ABI already settled for effects. `copy_from` exists because a handle cannot be assigned and the canonical type is copyable; the texture members are copied as borrows.  `operator==` and `operator!=` map to the single `_equals` route, and texture members compare **by identity** -- two sets are equal when they point at the same textures, not at equal ones. `GetHashCode` widens to `uint64_t`, the campaign's settled deviation. `ToString` takes the count/copy form and names only the active extensions, so a neutral set prints as two bytes.  **This type throws nowhere: all twenty-four setters correct, in three different shapes, and telling them apart is the whole contract.** Nine members clamp to zero-to-one (`std::clamp`, per channel for the three colours). Five use a **guarded assignment** -- `if (value >= bound) field = value;` -- which leaves the previous value in place, so an out-of-range write is a silent no-op rather than a value pinned to the bound; four guard at zero and `iridescenceIor` guards at **one**, because an index of refraction below one describes a medium light speeds up in. One, `attenuationDistance`, floors at zero with a ternary, writing the bound where its neighbours keep the old value. Nine texture members take no correction at all. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 20, which writes every scalar out of range at both ends and reads it back, so each of the three correction shapes is distinguished from the other two rather than assumed; asserts the colour clamps element-wise; round-trips a borrowed texture and proves binding one does not keep it alive; and checks equality, hash and `ToString` against a copy that is then made to differ by one field. Proved to execute by asserting the guarded setter clamps to zero and watching the exit code move to stage 20. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-087A`) |

#### `modules/graphics-ext/include/CNA/Graphics/PostProcessChain.hpp`

| ID | Line | Access/kind | C++ symbol | C mapping | Tests | Status |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CPP-F7CABD527BF2` | 38 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::PostProcessChain` | `cna_post_process_chain_*` over an owned handle. The target pool is a **counted borrow**: destroying the chain is refused while the pool handle is outstanding.  **`addOwnedPass` is the one route in the engine layer that consumes a handle a caller still holds, and the reason is worth stating.** The canonical signature takes a `std::unique_ptr`; this ABI holds its objects in `shared_ptr` and cannot release one, so a literal transfer is not expressible. Rather than fake it, the chain resource keeps the handed-over pass alive itself and registers it with the non-owning `addPass`. **The observable lifetime is identical** -- the pass lives exactly as long as the chain, `clear` releases it, and the caller's handle is released either way -- and it avoids the one thing a forced transfer risks, two owners of the same object. The route is named `add_owned_pass` rather than being a flag on `add_pass` precisely because the handle dies; a caller can see that in the name.  `PassTiming` carries a name, a duration and a sample count. A C structure cannot own the string, so the timing splits into a plain `CNA_PassTimingEXT` value and a separate `copy_pass_timing_name` -- the structure then has no lifetime of its own. Both canonical throws on `apply` are argument mistakes and are answered before the chain sees them, with separate messages: a context with no source has nothing to read from, and a non-positive size gives the chain nothing to allocate its intermediates against. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 26, which proves the borrowed pass stays usable after the chain records it and the **owned** pass's handle is genuinely dead afterwards -- asserted rather than documented, because a route promising ownership transfer that left the handle usable would invite a double free. It also refuses an index into an empty timing list, and asserts the pool borrow blocks destruction. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses. Proved to execute on both arms by asserting the consumed handle still answers, which moves the exit code to stage 26. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-089A`) |

| `CPP-2F226BBDCB64` | 29 | public struct | `CNA::Graphics::PostProcessContext` | `CNA_PostProcessContext` plus `cna_post_process_context_init`, a fixed-layout struct whose texture and target pointers become handles resolved and **retained for the duration of one apply**, so a pass cannot read a texture the caller released between filling the struct and applying it. `struct_size`/`struct_version` make an uninitialized context a refusal rather than a misreading.  **`settings` was the field this structure could not carry, and `CBIND-100` is why it now can.** `CBIND-084C` deferred it because binding it against a subset of the settings would have applied engine defaults for every omitted field; `CBIND-088B` could not add it either, because appending to this structure would have been refused by its own validator. With the prefix rule in place the field is appended as version 2 and bound as a **borrowed pointer**, matching the canonical `const RenderPipelineSettings*` exactly rather than copying a large value into every context. A version-1 caller's structure stops before it, passes `CNA_POST_PROCESS_CONTEXT_SIZE_V1`, and is accepted; CNA never reads past what `struct_size` declares. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` in both builds; the pass and material arms run wherever the layer is present and are proved to execute rather than fall through; `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 30, which applies a chain with a version-1 structure, with a larger-than-current one, and with settings attached, and refuses anything below the mandatory prefix | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-084C`) |

| `CPP-5CAB95E5A5DF` | 78 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::RenderPipeline` | `cna_render_pipeline_*` over an owned handle, with `FrameStatistics` as a versioned `CNA_RenderPipelineFrameStatisticsEXT`. Settings are copied in and out through `CNA_RenderPipelineSettingsEXT` -- the canonical getter returns a reference into the pipeline and the C form copies, so the result stays correct after the pipeline changes; writing them back runs every field through its canonical setter, so `CBIND-088A`'s thirty-one corrections apply here unchanged.  **The frame bracket was read before the test was written, because two other classes in this phase are not what they look like.** `RenderPipeline::begin` marks the frame open *before* any support check and `end` clears it *before* any early return, so the pair is symmetric on every renderer -- unlike `WeightedBlendedTransparency` and the shadow maps as they stood then (`CBIND-098`, `CBIND-097`; both have since been corrected in the engine layer, which is what makes this row's negative finding a finding rather than a coincidence). Both halves can therefore assert success rather than branching on support. A negative finding, but only because it was checked.  **Six throws, two kinds, and one pair the exception type cannot separate.** `invalid_argument` becomes `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT` (a non-positive size, an inverted or non-positive camera plane pair) and `logic_error` becomes `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE`. But `begin` throws `logic_error` for **two different states** -- a frame already open, and a pipeline that has never been sized -- and the pipeline exposes no width accessor to tell them apart after the fact. The C layer therefore remembers whether `resize` ever succeeded and answers the two with their own messages, which is work the binding does rather than something it inherits.  Both callback surfaces follow `CBIND-087D`'s rule: a failing draw stops the frame and its own result reaches the caller unchanged. The user pass and the shadow map are borrowed, never owned. Three rows are deferred with named owners: `setSkybox`/`getSkybox` to `CBIND-091`, which owns `Skybox`, and `getPassTimingsEXT` to `CBIND-089`, which owns `PostProcessChain::PassTiming`. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 25, which drives the whole frame lifecycle and asserts the two `begin` states separately -- never-sized before `resize`, already-open after a successful `begin` -- refuses releasing device resources mid-frame, proves an out-of-range setting written through the pipeline comes back corrected, and cross-checks every statistic against its individual accessor so a copy-paste error between the two readings shows up. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses. Proved to execute on both arms by asserting that a never-sized pipeline accepts `begin`, which moves the exit code to stage 25. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-088B`) |

| `CPP-52289B71749E` | 49 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::Skybox` | `cna_skybox_*` over its own owned handle. Support is probed at construction, and a skybox that cannot draw -- refused shader, or no environment -- **skips silently and still succeeds**: a missing sky is a scene without a sky, not a broken frame.  Two attach routes, because the canonical class has two. `set_environment` **borrows** (and releases an owned cube first, or attaching over one would keep it alive with nothing referring to it); `set_owned_environment` **consumes the handle**, following `cna_post_process_chain_add_owned_pass`, the campaign's settled shape for a canonical `unique_ptr` parameter. The transfer is done by releasing the handle -- the last step that can fail, so a refusal never leaves the caller holding nothing -- and retaining the cube on the resource.  `setIntensity` **floors at zero**, which is deliberately *not* what the identically named `AtmosphericSky` setter does. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 35: drawing with nothing attached is asserted to **succeed**, the borrowed getter handle is released twice over to show the cube survives it, and the consumed handle is asserted to be unusable afterwards. The floor is asserted against the atmospheric sky's guard in the same stage, so a binding that regularized the two would fail exactly one of them. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-091B`) |

| `CPP-43DDC2874473` | 43 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::SpatialUpscalePass` | One `cna_<pass>_create` each plus the pass's own accessors, on `CBIND-089B`'s helpers.  **Two of the nine are not passes, and finding that out was the slice.** `DecalPass` and `SpatialUpscalePass` are named "Pass" and were counted among the seventeen, but neither derives from `PostProcessPass`: they have no `apply`, and each is driven by its own `draw` with explicit sizes rather than by a chain. The compiler said so -- their `shared_ptr` would not convert -- which is the only reason it was caught before the shape was wrong in the ABI. They carry their own handles (`CNA_DecalPassHandle`, `CNA_SpatialUpscalePassHandle`), their own object kinds and their own destroy, and the shared `cna_post_process_pass_*` routes correctly **refuse** them.  `AsciiPass::getEffect` lends the pass's own effect. Binding it needed the resource type behind `CNA_AsciiPostProcessEffectHandle` to be **shared between two translation units** rather than redeclared: two units that register or read one `ObjectKind` must agree on the type it holds, and a second local declaration would compile, register under the same kind, and then be cast to the wrong type -- undefined behaviour no test would reliably catch. `AsciiEffectResource` moved to `CnaCApiGraphicsExtDetail.hpp` for that reason, which is a deliberate structural change rather than a side effect.  **`FxaaPass` corrects nothing**, while the settings bag that can drive the same number floors it at `CNA_RENDER_PIPELINE_MINIMUM_FXAA_EDGE_THRESHOLD_EXT`. Two surfaces, one value, only one correcting -- asserted on both rather than assumed consistent. `DecalPass::setCamera` ignores a non-positive far plane by guarding the whole assignment, so the previous camera survives. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 29, which asserts the shared pass routes **refuse** the two standalone objects and accept the seven real passes -- the only way a caller learns the difference from outside. Proved to execute by asserting the shared destroy accepts a `DecalPass`, which moves the exit code to stage 29 on both arms. Every correcting field is written out of range at both ends against its own bound; `FxaaPass`'s free field is checked against the settings bag's floor in the same stage. The ASCII effect borrow is taken, released, and the pass then still answers. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-089D`) |

Everything the three share -- `apply`, `getName`, `isSupported`, destruction -- is already bound by `CBIND-084` on the `CNA_PostProcessPassHandle`, so those rows map to routes that exist rather than to new ones. **A pass-specific accessor is refused by argument, not by handle, when the handle names another pass**: the handle is perfectly valid, it is the concrete type that cannot answer, which is the rule `CBIND-085B1` settled for interfaces.  Two internal helpers carry the shape for the rest of the phase: `CreateEnginePass<T>` and `WithEnginePass<T>`. `CBIND-089C` and `CBIND-089D` reuse them unchanged, which is what makes thirteen more passes a table rather than thirteen more designs.  **Three correction shapes, and the bounds differ between fields of the same pass.** `SsrPass` clamps its roughness blur to `0..0.25` and its edge fade to `0..0.5`, and guards three more with `if (value > 0)`, which leaves the previous value in place rather than pinning to the bound. `DepthOfFieldPass` guards three and clamps one. **`SsaoPass` corrects nothing at all** -- established by reading the four setter bodies, not by the file-level grep, which counted five corrections in that file that all live in `apply()` rather than in a setter. That is the same blind spot `CBIND-087A` recorded, in the opposite direction: a grep that over-counts is as misleading as one that under-counts.  `kMinStepCount`/`kMaxStepCount` become macros, and the setter deliberately does **not** enforce them: the march clamps the count where it applies it, so a caller reads back what it wrote. That is the canonical convention this campaign has now met three times -- the passes clamp what they apply, so the settings never silently change a number a caller can read. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 27, which asserts **each bound on its own** -- proved to matter by asserting the edge fade clamps to its neighbour's 0.25 instead of its own 0.5, which moves the exit code to stage 27 on both arms. Each guarded setter gets the extra half a clamp does not need: a valid value first, then an out-of-range write that must leave the valid one in place. The free fields are written out of range and must survive, the step count past its own documented maximum. The packed and unpacked occlusion GLSL must differ, or the flag is ignored; Low and Ultra must ask for different sample counts, or the preset does nothing; and the circle of confusion must be exactly zero at the focus distance and grow away from it in both directions. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-089B`) |

#### `modules/graphics-ext/include/CNA/Graphics/TransparentDrawList.hpp`

| ID | Line | Access/kind | C++ symbol | C mapping | Tests | Status |

| `CPP-C35426C4C2E3` | 48 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::VolumetricFogPass` | One `cna_<pass>_create` each plus the pass's own accessors, on `CBIND-089B`'s `CreateEnginePass<T>`/`WithEnginePass<T>` helpers reused unchanged -- which is what makes four more passes a table rather than four more designs. The shared base stays with `CBIND-084`; the three per-pass constants become macros with a `static_assert`.  **The guards here are not interchangeable, and that is the whole slice.** Four setters guard with `if (value >= 0)` and **accept zero** -- no fog, no shafts and no aerial perspective are all legitimate settings -- while `VolumetricFogPass::setRange` and `HeightFogPass::setFalloff` guard with `if (value > 0)` and **reject zero as well**, because a zero range has no volume to march and a zero falloff is a division by zero. A shared "negatives are ignored" reading would have got two of the six wrong.  Two more bounds are unusual enough to name. `setTurbidity` floors at **one**, not zero: turbidity is a ratio against a perfectly clear atmosphere, so below one describes air clearer than vacuum. `setAnisotropy` clamps to **-0.95 through 0.95** -- the only two-sided clamp in this phase with a negative lower bound, because scattering runs from fully backward to fully forward and both poles are singular. `HeightFogPass::setBaseHeight` corrects nothing, because a fog base below the origin is legitimate.  `setLight` takes a borrowed shadow map; `CNA_INVALID_HANDLE` means march unshadowed rather than being an error. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 28, which asserts each guard's own bound -- a valid value, then zero, then a negative -- so the `>= 0` and `> 0` guards are told apart rather than assumed alike. Proved to matter by asserting the range guard admits zero the way the density beside it does, which moves the exit code to stage 28 on both arms. The three pure functions are checked by their **relationships** rather than by duplicating their maths: air mass grows with distance, transmittance falls as air mass grows, and optical depth is exactly zero at zero distance and grows with both distance and density. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-089C`) |

| `CPP-1E294DBD144B` | 61 | public class | `CNA::Graphics::WeightedBlendedTransparency` | `cna_weighted_blended_transparency_*` over an owned handle. Both targets are borrowed and exist exactly when the resolve does.  **The eight canonical throws are two different mistakes and are kept apart.** `invalid_argument` becomes `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT` and `logic_error` becomes `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE`, because a caller acts on them differently: fix the number, or fix the order of the calls. Flattening them -- which the firewall would do unaided -- would tell a caller that a size of zero and a bracket left open are the same error. Both are checked ahead of the canonical call so the result is decided here rather than recovered from an exception type.  `weight` clamps twice, and both are **corrections**: the curve is unbounded near zero depth, and a weight that overflows would poison the whole accumulation buffer rather than one fragment.  **`begin` opens the bracket on every renderer**, so `is_accumulating` reports true and the matching `end` succeeds whether or not the resolve can run; what the unsupported path skips is the device work, not the bracket, and `end` then restores nothing rather than resetting states the caller owns. It did not always: through `CBIND-098` `begin` returned before opening the bracket wherever the resolve was unsupported, so a correctly paired `end` refused with "accumulation is not open" and the object stayed unusable afterwards. Fixed in the canonical engine layer on 2026-08-28 under an owner exception to this campaign's audit-only rule, with the C test that used to pin the defect changed to assert the contract. | `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 23, which asserts the argument and state refusals are different results, exercises every sequencing mistake while the bracket is open, and asserts the same bracket contract on both sides of `is_supported` -- begin succeeds, `is_accumulating` reports true, the matching end succeeds, a second end is refused and the pass survives a completed bracket -- with only the in-bracket behaviour differing. It used to pin `CBIND-098` here instead; the canonical fix is covered by `WeightedBlendedTransparencyTest.TheBracketIsSymmetricOnEveryRenderer`, which was mutation-checked by restoring the old ordering and watching it fail. Proved to execute on both branches by inverting the accumulating assertion and watching the exit code move to stage 23 on EasyGL and on HEADLESS alike. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-087D`) |

| `CPP-48AD8245DB54` | 19 | public class | `CNA::Input::Clipboard` | `cna_clipboard_get_text_size`/`cna_clipboard_copy_text` for the read, `cna_clipboard_set_text` taking a borrowed UTF-8 view, and `cna_clipboard_get_has_text`. The canonical setter returns nothing and therefore reports no platform outcome, and the C route reproduces that rather than inventing one: **success means the request was made, not that the clipboard changed**, since a headless session or a gesture-gated browser may ignore it. The clipboard is process-external state, so the count is documented as a hint and every copy reports its own byte count | `InputDevicesSmoke.c` captures the pre-existing clipboard, probes with non-ASCII UTF-8, and asserts a **relationship** rather than a fixed answer — if the write took effect the read must return exactly those bytes, and the presence flag must agree with a non-empty read in both directions — then proves the empty-clipboard and buffer-too-small cases only on a platform that actually stored the text, refuses malformed UTF-8, and restores the original content because this is state the suite does not own | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037B7b`) |

#### `modules/input/include/CNA/Input/HapticDevice.hpp`

| ID | Line | Access/kind | C++ symbol | C mapping | Tests | Status |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CPP-B18D9C96B10A` | 33 | public class | `CNA::Input::HapticDevice` | an owned `CNA_HapticDeviceHandle`. The canonical destructor becomes `cna_haptic_device_destroy` and `Dispose` its own idempotent route, so a caller can close the device without giving up the handle — the same split `MouseCursor` uses. A closed device is not an error state: every route on it succeeds and answers `CNA_FALSE`, zero or -1 through its output, which is what makes the family usable with no force-feedback hardware. Two canonical pass-throughs are preserved: the rumble strength, the gain and the autocenter are handed to the platform unvalidated, and freeing an unknown effect identifier is a successful no-op because the canonical operation reports nothing. `RunEffectEXT`'s defaulted iteration count is passed explicitly, since C has no defaulted arguments | `HapticsSmoke.c` drives every route on a closed device and on any real device the machine supplies, asserts the -1 effect identifier and the false answers a closed device must give, proves disposal is idempotent and leaves the handle usable, and covers double release, a never-created handle and every null-output refusal, under HEADLESS, SDL_RENDERER and SOFTWARE plus ASan+UBSan with leak detection on | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037B6`) |

| `CPP-ED102D017D48` | 22 | public class | `CNA::Input::Haptics` | free `cna_haptics_*` routes rather than a handle, because the canonical constructor is deleted and every member is static — the same shape as `Mouse`, `Keyboard`, `TextInputEXT` and `TouchPanel`. | `CPP-0A6DB47508CC` | 17 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Input::Mouse` | one `cna_mouse_*` route per canonical static, each taking an active game handle. The class itself has no handle: its canonical constructor is deleted and every member is static. The window handle crosses as an opaque `uint64_t` the C API never dereferences, not as a `CNA_Handle`. A request no backend can satisfy answers `CNA_FALSE` through an applied output rather than failing, and `GetGlobalPositionEXT` — which the canonical API declares `void` with two output references — reports both coordinates and cannot fail. `INTERNAL_onClicked` becomes `cna_mouse_raise_clicked_ext`, which is what makes the clicked event observable without a real device, and `ResetForTests` becomes `_reset_for_tests_ext`, documented as clearing the bound window and dropping every subscription including ones this API handed out | `InputSnapshotsSmoke.c` round-trips the window handle and restores it, exercises position, capture, global position, warp and relative mode with their null-output refusals, raises a click and observes it, and proves the reset drops a live subscription so the handler stops running and the registration release afterwards is still a success, under HEADLESS, SDL_RENDERER and SOFTWARE | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037B4b`) |

| `CPP-96F2229DA75C` | 36 | public constructor | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Quaternion::Quaternion()` | the zero-initialized `CNA_Quaternion`. The canonical parameterless constructor sets all four components to zero -- C# gives every struct one that zeroes its fields, and the canonical comment says so -- and the C form of that is the struct's own zero value, which a caller writes directly in a declaration. An init route would be a second spelling of it.  **Read rather than assumed**, because `CBIND-081` recorded the same trap for `Matrix()`: the friendly-looking default for a quaternion is the *identity*, and it is not what the canonical constructor produces. | `QuaternionSmoke.c` `validate_default_value` requires a zeroed `CNA_Quaternion` to be (0,0,0,0) and the identity from `cna_quaternion_get_identity` to be (0,0,0,1), then requires the two to differ -- which is what would fail if a later change made the C default the friendlier identity. Mutation-checked: setting the zeroed value's `w` to 1 fails. | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-103`) |

| `CPP-BEAB0FE122E9` | 20 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Media::Album` | a borrowed `CNA_AlbumHandle` with the name count/copy pair, duration in ticks, the songs collection, and `cna_album_equals`, whose rule is **not** name alone: album names collide across artists, so the canonical comparison pairs the name with the artist, and two albums with no artist match on the name. The artist and genre are optional, so they follow the availability-separate-from-the-answer rule rather than failing. **The two art members return a stream whose caller owns it; no stream crosses this ABI** — `cna_album_get_art_size`/`_copy_art` and the thumbnail pair read that stream to its end and destroy it inside the call, so the image crosses as bytes. The thumbnail is the same image as the cover, which is canonical behavior rather than a C limitation, and both refuse an album without art with `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE` | `MediaLibrarySmoke.c` points SDL's user-folder lookup at a generated fixture through `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, so the library it scans is deterministic — two tag-only MP3 files sharing an artist, album and genre, plus a folder cover image — instead of whatever music the host happens to hold, and no real user directory is ever read or written. The album's name, duration, artist, genre and two-song collection are all asserted against the fixture's tags, and the art and thumbnail routes are proven to return **exactly** the twelve fixture cover bytes, with the buffer-too-small case writing nothing | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037C3`) |

#### `modules/media/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Media/MediaPlayer.hpp`

| ID | Line | Access/kind | C++ symbol | C mapping | Tests | Status |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CPP-187387966869` | 22 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Media::MediaPlayer` | free `cna_media_player_*` routes, because C has no static class. Every route takes an active game handle for the same reason the input captures do — the player is process-wide state a running game owns. The three `Play` overloads become `_play_song`, `_play_songs` and `_play_songs_from`; **the canonical player copies the song it is given into its queue rather than taking it**, so a caller's handle is unaffected. Two canonical behaviors are preserved rather than tightened: the volume setter **clamps** to 0 through 1 instead of refusing, and the indexed `Play` overload does not range-check its index. The two static `EventHandler` events become owned registrations with one shared `cna_media_player_unsubscribe_ext`, and the canonical deferred raises are exposed as `_raise_active_song_changed_ext`/`_raise_media_state_changed_ext` so a C application can observe its own wiring. `Update`, `ProgramExit` and the elapsed-time song-end detector keep `_ext` suffixes, being CNA extensions; the detector's canonical rule is preserved exactly — a song whose duration is unknown never reports ended | `MediaPlayerSmoke.c` round-trips every flag and restores it, since these are process-wide settings the suite does not own; proves the volume clamp at both ends; drives the queue through `play`, `pause`, `resume` and `stop` asserting the transitions **as a relationship** — whether playback actually starts depends on the platform's ability to decode the file, not on the C API, so the suite asserts the paused/playing round trip only when playback began and the no-op contract otherwise; covers both event registrations end to end with per-registration detach; and proves the song-end detector reports nothing for an unknown duration and reports ended once a known one is exceeded | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037C6`) |

| `CPP-43541AECFE4D` | 16 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Media::MediaQueue` | a borrowed `CNA_MediaQueueHandle` from `cna_media_player_get_queue` — a view of the one process-lifetime queue, like a stock mouse cursor — with count, active index get/set, `_get_at`, `_get_active_song`, `_add`, `_clear` and a type-name pair. **Two deliberate deviations, both forced by ownership.** A queue entry crosses as an *independently owned copy* rather than a borrowed view, because the canonical queue destroys its entries whenever it is cleared — which every play route does — so a borrowed handle would dangle; the copy carries the same file and name and therefore compares equal to the entry. And `cna_media_queue_add` appends a *copy* too, because the canonical `Add` adopts the pointer it is given and C cannot hand a handle's object away without leaving the caller a stale handle — appending a copy is exactly what the canonical player itself does when it enqueues a song. The active index setter stores its value unchecked, as the canonical one does | `MediaPlayerSmoke.c` proves the empty queue's -1 active index and unavailable active song, that appending leaves the caller's handle working and yields an entry equal to it, that an out-of-range index is refused in both directions, the exact type name, and that clearing empties the queue | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037C6`) |

| `CPP-C02460FB385B` | 16 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Media::SongCollection` | an owned `CNA_SongCollectionHandle` built from an array of song handles, with `cna_song_collection_get_at` for the canonical indexer, `_get_count`, `_get_is_disposed`, `_dispose`, `_destroy` and the type-name count/copy pair. **The collection retains every song it was given**: the canonical collection stores non-owning pointers, so C keeps the song resources alive beside it rather than letting a released handle leave a dangling element behind — a caller may release its own song handles immediately after building one. `cna_song_collection_get_at` hands back a new handle sharing the collection's song rather than a copy. The canonical disposal is preserved exactly: it **empties** the collection, so afterwards the count is zero and every index is out of range, while the songs themselves are untouched. #### `modules/media/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Media/Video/VideoPlayer.hpp`

|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CPP-202000FD20E2` | 44 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Media::VideoPlayer` | an owned `CNA_VideoPlayerHandle` with the loop, mute, volume, position, state and video properties, the four transport routes, both track selectors, and the canonical dispose-versus-release split. **The frame texture is the slice's one hard problem, and it is solved by lifetime rather than by copying**: the player owns and replaces its frame texture, so `cna_video_player_get_texture` hands back a borrowed `CNA_Texture2DHandle` that the C layer itself **invalidates on the next call to that player** — any later route, including another `get_texture`, releases it, so a stale frame handle fails with `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_HANDLE` instead of touching freed memory. Asking before playback is an ordinary `CNA_FALSE`, because the canonical implementation deliberately answers null there where the original API faults. Playing a file the platform cannot decode leaves the player stopped rather than failing, and disposal makes every playback route report the canonical disposed-object failure while the disposal query keeps answering. The C resource retains the video it was told to play, so releasing the caller's video handle can never leave the player pointing at a destroyed video | `VideoSmoke.c` covers creation, every property round trip, the no-frame answer before playback, playing an undecodable file leaving the player stopped, the played video reported back, transport calls in every state, releasing the caller's video handle while the player still holds it, and disposal turning every playback route into `INVALID_STATE` while the disposal query still answers | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037C7`) |

| `CPP-CC7A579829D2` | 6 | public struct | `CNA::RuntimeOptions` | No C mapping, and the reason is not a design choice: **`CNA::Runtime` is declared and defined nowhere**. All five of its methods would fail to link if anything called them, nothing in the tree calls them, no translation unit includes `CNA/Misc.hpp`, and the compiled runtime archive contains no `CNA::Runtime::` symbol at all — the repository's own `audit/include/CNA/Misc.hpp.audit.md` reached the same conclusion independently. This ABI cannot bind a symbol that does not exist. `RuntimeOptions` is a sound four-flag value on its own, but its only purpose is to parameterize `Initialize`, so mapping it alone would hand a C consumer a structure that configures nothing. | `CPP-E71425DB675F` | 23 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::GameComponent` | an owned `CNA_GameComponentHandle` from `cna_game_component_create`, with the enabled and update-order pairs, `cna_game_component_initialize`/`_update`/`_dispose`/`_compare_to`, the type-name pair, `cna_game_component_subscribe` for all three events and `cna_game_component_destroy`. Two canonical behaviors are preserved rather than corrected: **the comparison subtracts this component's order from the other's**, so the component that updates earlier compares greater, and a **second disposal is a no-op** — the opposite of a sensor's refusal, and this type's own idempotence. | `CPP-EB2A95C9E294` | 38 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::GameWindow` | `cna_game_window_*` routes on the game handle: the resizing pair, the client bounds, the current orientation as the existing `CNA_DisplayOrientation` identity, the display-name and title count/copy pairs, the borderless pair, minimize and restore, the screen-device-change bracket, a type-name pair and `cna_game_window_subscribe` for all three events. Two canonical shapes collapse: the platform handle property and the native-window accessor answer the **same pointer**, so C has one route, and the name-only screen-device-change overload is the sized one with the current client size, so a non-positive size means keep it. Creating the manager **registers both services**, which is what `cna_game_services_contains_ext` then reports, and a game accepts exactly one. Every reconfiguration reports `CNA_RESULT_PLATFORM` when the platform declines, the rule the window slice established. **Releasing a manager keeps the object alive until its game is destroyed**: the canonical game caches a raw pointer to the graphics device service and never clears it, so destroying the manager first would leave the game dereferencing freed memory on its next frame — a canonical defect this ABI works around rather than exposes | `GraphicsDeviceManagerSmoke.c` creates the manager and asserts both services appear, refuses a second manager, round-trips every preference and refuses every undefined identity, proves the orientation bit set accepts a combination, borrows the managed device, applies the changes and re-creates the device accepting a platform refusal as correct, runs the draw bracket, asserts disposal unregisters both services and raises its event exactly once across two disposals, and covers every released-handle refusal. The retained-object rule is proved by the suite running clean under ASan, where the earlier design reproduced a heap-use-after-free on the very next frame | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037E4`) |
